title: Stories, reimagined through AI.
introduction: An independent creative practice exploring the intersection of artificial intelligence, filmmaking, and visual storytelling. From cinematic AI films and brand advertisements to experimental narratives and digital experiences, I create visuals that bring ambitious ideas to life.
biography:
I am an AI filmmaker and creative producer passionate about pushing the boundaries of visual storytelling through emerging technologies. My work combines creative conceptualisation, filmmaking principles, and generative AI to develop cinematic advertisements, narrative films, microdramas, and immersive visual experiences.

With a background in broadcast journalism, media production, and performing arts, I bring a storytelling-first approach to every project. I enjoy experimenting with new creative technologies, developing distinctive visual identities, and transforming ideas into compelling audiovisual experiences.
background:
My creative journey spans journalism, media production, digital content creation, and filmmaking. Over the years, I have explored different aspects of storytelling, from editorial development and video production to cinematography, editing, and sound.

Today, my focus lies in AI-powered filmmaking and creative production. I work across the entire creative process, including concept development, scriptwriting, visual direction, prompt engineering, character development, AI image and video generation, and post-production. I am particularly interested in maintaining visual consistency, cinematic realism, and narrative continuity across AI-generated productions.
philosophy:
Technology is the medium. Storytelling is the purpose.

I believe AI should expand creative possibilities, not replace creative thinking. Every frame should have an intention, every visual should serve the narrative, and every experiment should push the boundaries of what is possible. My approach is rooted in curiosity, cinematic thinking, and the pursuit of meaningful visual storytelling.
